definitions.explanation: a horticultural technique where a cutting from one plant (scion) is inserted into another plant (rootstock) so they grow together as one

examples.japanese: {果樹|かじゅ}は{接|つ}ぎ{木|き}で{増|ふ}やすことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Fruit trees are often propagated by grafting.

examples.japanese: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}をすると{病気|びょうき}に{強|つよ}い{木|き}が{作|つく}れる。
examples.english: By grafting, you can create trees that are resistant to disease.

examples.japanese: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}は{古代|こだい}から{使|つか}われてきた。
examples.english: Grafting techniques have been used since ancient times.

notes:
USAGE:
{接|つ}ぎ{木|き} is essential in fruit tree cultivation, allowing farmers to combine desired fruit characteristics (scion) with a hardy root system (rootstock). Can also be used as a verb: {接|つ}ぎ{木|き}する.

ADVANTAGES OF GRAFTING:
- Combines disease-resistant rootstocks with high-quality fruit varieties
- Produces fruit faster than growing from seed
- Maintains exact genetic characteristics of the parent plant

RELATED TERMS:
- {台木|だいぎ} (rootstock)
- {穂木|ほぎ} (scion)
- {挿|さ}し{木|き} (cutting propagation)
